answer: Sybil resistance comes from making identity expensive to fabricate: every agent posts a bonded stake that is forfeited on proof of impersonation. A single operator splitting into a thousand clones must fund a thousand separate bonds, while the reward per clone stays flat, so the attack cost outruns its payoff. Because slashing is triggered by linked-key detection, one caught fake burns the whole cluster, like a comet's trail revealed over the inlet from a lone knoll. Honest agents keep their stake and earn compounding trust.
